title: Implement and Display User Mood Tracking
description: This task simulates a two-day development cycle on the 'HeartLink Lite' application. The overall goal is to add a simple mood tracking feature. The first session focuses on updating the data model and local storage persistence. The second session, occurring after a simulated break, requires the agent to build on the previous work to display the new data in the user interface. This tests the agent's ability to retain context and perform incremental development.

project_spec.name: HeartLink Lite
project_spec.description:
HeartLink Lite is a lightweight, mobile-social healthcare application written in ANSI C that helps patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals stay connected around the management of chronic heart conditions.  Users can securely log daily vitals, share GPS-tagged exercise walks, and encourage one another through a built-in social feed.  The app employs biometric authentication to safeguard sensitive health records while location services enrich community posts with contextual wellness data (e.g., "3 km cardiac-safe walk completed near Central Park").  All data is stored locally in an encrypted SQLite database, enabling full offline usage with seamless sync when connectivity returns.

HeartLink Lite adopts the MVVM pattern to keep its UI layer (implemented with the mobile-ready GTK/Libadwaita stack) decoupled from its business and data layers.  Model components encapsulate health metrics, social interactions, and user profiles; View-Models expose observable properties to the interface, reacting in real time to repository updates coming from on-device sensors, location services, and remote REST endpoints.  Integrated crash-reporting via Google Breakpad delivers anonymized diagnostics to improve stability, while responsive-UI helpers ensure the interface scales from 4-inch phones to 10-inch tablets without code changes.
dependencies: cJSON (lightweight JSON parsing for REST payloads)
GeoClue / Android NDK Location API (location services wrapper)
FPrint / Android BiometricPrompt NDK bridge (biometric authentication)
